We need propose retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction for target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Interpret: It's a bicyclic? Looks like a cyclopentane fused? Actually there is a phenyl attached to an exocyclic alkene with a cyclopentanol bearing CF3? Wait C15 with three Fs is CF3 attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13? The structure: an alkene CH2= C(aryl) - chiral carbon attached to cyclopentane ring with OH and CF3 substituent.

The retrosynthesis: carbonyl-ene reaction forward: carbonyl + alkene -> product with new C-C bond, OH, and ring formation. So reverse: break C-O bond (alcohol) to carbonyl, break C-C bond formed, form C=C and C=O. So precursor would be a ketone (or aldehyde) and an alkene that undergoes intramolecular ene? Actually carbonyl-ene can be intramolecular where carbonyl and alkene in same molecule form new bond and generate cyclic alcohol. So reverse: we need a molecule that is a cyclopentane with carbonyl (maybe ketone) and an alkene side chain that can undergo ene to give the product.

Our target has a cyclopentane ring (5-member) with OH at carbon 13 (attached to carbon 13). In forward ene, the OH is formed at carbonyl carbon after reaction. So precursor would have a carbonyl at that position (C=O) instead of OH, and the alkene would be external (CH2= C(aryl)?) Actually the alkene is the exocyclic double bond attached to carbon 2 (C=). In product, that double bond is now single bond between C2 and C9? Wait product: CH2= C(aryl) - C* (C9) attached to cyclopentane. So the double bond is between C1 and C2. In product, C2 is attached to aryl and to C9 (sp3). In precursor, likely C2 is part of alkene with CH2, and C9 is carbonyl carbon? Let's think: carbonyl-ene: carbonyl (C=O) reacts with alkene (C=C) where allylic hydrogen transfers to carbonyl oxygen forming OH, and new C-C bond forms between carbonyl carbon and alkene's terminal carbon (the one bearing H). The double bond shifts to internal position.

Thus product: carbonyl carbon becomes alcohol (C-OH) and attached to former alkene carbon (which now is sp3). The double bond moves to between the other two alkene carbons.

Our product has CH2= C(aryl) - C* (attached to ring). So the double bond is between CH2 and C (C2). The C* is attached to ring and originally was the carbonyl carbon? In ene, the carbonyl carbon attaches to the allylic carbon (the one bearing H). The double bond moves to between the other alkene carbon and the allylic carbon? Actually typical ene: R-CH=CH2 + R'CHO -> R-CH-CH2-CH(OH)-R' (new sigma bond between CH2 carbon and carbonyl carbon, double bond shifts to between CH and CH). So product has new C-C bond between carbonyl carbon and terminal alkene carbon, and double bond now internal.

Thus our product: CH2= C(aryl) - C* (attached to ring). The new bond is between C* and the carbonyl carbon precursor. So C* is carbonyl carbon in precursor. The double bond in product is between CH2 and C(aryl). In precursor, the alkene would be between C(aryl) and something else? Actually the double bond shifts: In product, double bond is between CH2 and C(aryl). In precursor, the double bond would be between C(aryl) and the carbonyl carbon? Wait typical: starting alkene: A= B-CH2 (where B is internal carbon). After ene, product: A-CH-CH2-CH(OH)-R (new bond between carbonyl carbon and CH2). Double bond now between A and CH (former internal carbon). So the double bond moves one position towards the carbonyl.

Thus our product double bond between CH2 (C1) and C(aryl) (C2). So precursor double bond would be between C(aryl) (C2) and C* (carbonyl carbon). So precursor would have a carbonyl attached directly to C2 via double bond (i.e., an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl). That seems plausible: an α,β-unsaturated ketone where carbonyl carbon is attached to cyclopentane (with CF3) and double bond to C2 which is attached to aryl and CH2.

Thus precursor: a cyclopentanone (with OH replaced by =O) at carbon 13 (C13) attached to C2 via double bond (C2= C(=O)-). The aryl attached to C2, and CH2 attached to C2 as exocyclic? Actually CH2 is attached to C2 as part of double bond: CH2=C(aryl)-C(=O)-cyclopentane. So precursor SMILES: C= C(c1ccccc1)C(=O)C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1O? Wait OH removed, carbonyl present, but the cyclopentane still has OH? In precursor, the OH is carbonyl O, not OH. So the cyclopentane carbon bearing carbonyl is carbonyl carbon, not bearing OH. So the cyclopentane would be a ketone attached to the ring (i.e., a cyclopentanone). The ring also has CF3 substituent at adjacent carbon? In product, CF3 attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13 (the carbon bearing OH). In precursor, carbon 15 attached to carbonyl carbon (C13) as same. So we have a cyclopentanone with CF3 substituent at the carbon adjacent to carbonyl? Actually carbon 13 is carbonyl carbon, attached to CF3 carbon (C15) which is attached to three Fs. So the carbonyl carbon is attached to CF3 carbon (i.e., carbonyl carbon attached to a carbon bearing three Fs). That's a carbonyl attached to a CF3-substituted carbon (i.e., a carbonyl adjacent to CF3). So the precursor is α-CF3 cyclopentanone? Wait carbonyl carbon attached to CF3 carbon (C15) which is sp3 with three Fs. So the carbonyl carbon is attached to that carbon (C15). So the carbonyl carbon is part of the ring, and the CF3 carbon is attached to the carbonyl carbon as a side chain.

Thus precursor SMILES: C= C(c1ccccc1)C(=O)C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1 . No OH.

Let's construct: CH2= C(aryl) C(=O) attached to cyclopentane. The cyclopentane: C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1 (a cyclopentane with CF3 substituent). The carbonyl carbon is part of the ring: so we need a cyclopentanone: O=C- attached to two ring carbons. So SMILES: O=C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1 . Then attach the α,β-unsaturated side chain at the carbonyl carbon? Actually the carbonyl carbon is part of ring, cannot have extra substituent besides the two ring bonds and the carbonyl O. In product, carbonyl carbon (C13) is attached to ring (two bonds) and to C2 (new bond). In precursor, carbonyl carbon is attached to ring (two bonds) and double bond to C2 (α,β-unsaturated). So carbonyl carbon is part of conjugated enone: O=C(-)C(=C(...))? Wait carbonyl carbon double bonded to O, single bond to C2 (alkenyl), and also part of ring (two bonds). That's impossible because carbonyl carbon can have only three sigma bonds: one to O (double counts as 2), one to C2, and one to ring carbon. Actually carbonyl carbon is sp2, attached to O (double), attached to C2 (single), attached to one ring carbon (single). The other ring bond is to adjacent carbon in ring (makes the ring). So carbonyl carbon is part of ring as a carbonyl (cyclopentanone). The side chain attaches at carbonyl carbon as exocyclic double bond (enone). So the precursor is an α,β-unsaturated cyclopentanone with CF3 substituent on the carbon adjacent to carbonyl (maybe at position 2). So SMILES: C= C(c1ccccc1)C(=O)C1CCC(C(F)(F)F)C1 . That seems correct.

Now we need to propose retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction: the carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular) forward. So retrosynthetic step: target -> precursor (the enone). So we need to output JSON with root molecule target, child reaction with template_id (need to find appropriate template). We don't know template IDs. Could search. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken = ["alcohol"], functional_groups_formed = ["alkene"], bonds_order_changed maybe "C=O to C-O". Let's try.


We will call search_template_catalog_by_criteria.
